en.title: One week, 670 km² more white ground in Slovenia
en.description: Snow cover jumped from 90 km² to 760 km² in seven days. Fresh snow peaked at 30 cm in the high mountains on 19 November.
en.lede: Slovenia's high ground turned white fast this week: 670 km² more than seven days ago. The jump came from one strong cold spell that brought up to 30 cm of fresh snow to the mountains above 1,500 m.

p: A week ago, only 90 km² of Slovenia's mapped high ground held snow. By 16 November that had grown to 1,130 km². Then a thaw cut it back to 260 km² by 18 November. The cold returned, and by 19 November snow covered 760 km² again—a net gain of 670 km² since the week began.
This kind of swing is normal in early November: warm spells melt thin snow from lower slopes, cold snaps rebuild it. What matters now is whether the base lasts.

The Julian Alps got the most: 55 cm of fresh snow in three days. The Kamnik-Savinja Alps picked up 46 cm. Pohorje, in the east, saw only 3 cm. About 400 km² received at least 5 cm, mostly above 1,500 m.
The single wettest day was 22 November, with up to 17 cm. This was the first snow of the season in many spots.

Height decides everything. Below 1,000 m, almost no snow yet (1 % covered, under 1 cm average). Between 1,000 and 1,500 m, thin patches (13 % covered, under 1 cm). Between 1,500 and 2,000 m, a real base now: 9 cm average, 96 % covered. Above 2,000 m, solid: 25 cm average, fully white.
The snow line sits at about 1,400 m. Ski runs above that height have continuous cover. Below it, grass still shows through.

Kranjska Gora holds the deepest snow of Slovenia's resorts: 29 cm. This is ahead of normal for late November (usually 2 cm on this date). It picked up 7 cm in the last three days and could gain 9 cm more by Sunday 22 November.

Sella Nevea, higher up at 2,137 m, has 24 cm—way above its typical 2 cm for mid-November. It absorbed 28 cm in three days, an unusually big fall for this small resort. Up to 19 cm more is forecast before Sunday.

The rest: Vogel (12 cm, 8 cm in three days, 17 cm ahead), Kope (11 cm, 2 cm in three days, 9 cm ahead), Krvavec (8 cm, 17 cm in three days, 22 cm ahead). Snow sits on the upper slopes of 14 of Slovenia's 27 resorts.

The outlook for the week ahead: up to 35 cm total, with 17 cm in the next three days. After 22 November, the snow pace slows. Days 8 to 14 of the forecast (late November into early December) show up to 24 cm on the wettest slopes.

Early-season snow is thin and sits on bare rock in many places. Runs that are groomed and tracked are safest. Fresh snow on cold ground can be unstable on steep terrain: check the local avalanche bulletin before going off-piste.

sections.h: How this compares with Austria and Italy
p: Across the border, Austria is much whiter: 48 % of its high ground covered, with Stubaier Gletscher showing 74 cm. Italy sits at 27 % white, led by La Thuile ski at 66 cm. Slovenia at 10 % is behind both neighbours, but the gap will close if the forecast holds.

advice: Stick to groomed runs for now: the base under early snow is thin and may hide rocks.
If you plan to ski off-piste, read the local avalanche bulletin first. Fresh cold snow can slide on steep slopes.
Wait until after 22 November if you can: the new snow will have settled and roads will be cleared.
Above 1,500 m you will find continuous cover; below 1,000 m expect bare patches.
Pack a map: the thaw and refreeze mean snow cover is patchy at middle heights (1,000–1,500 m), with only 13 % white.

captions.new: Fresh snow fell across Slovenia in the three days to 19 November, peaking at 30 cm in the Julian Alps and Kamnik-Savinja Alps.
captions.map: Snow cover on 19 November: 760 km² of Slovenia's high ground (10 %), concentrated above 1,400 m. Seven days earlier only 90 km² was white.
captions.story: The week's swing: snow covered 1,130 km² on 16 November, dropped to 260 km² by 18 November as temperatures rose, then rebounded to 760 km² as the cold returned.

sl.title: Sneg v Sloveniji danes: višina snežne odeje in novi sneg, 19. novembra 2026
sl.description: Snežna pokrajnost se je povečala s 90 km² na 760 km² v sedmih dneh. Sveži sneg je dosegel vrh 30 cm v visokogorju 19. novembra.
sl.lede: Slovensko visokogorje se je ta teden hitro pobeljilo: 670 km² več kot pred sedmimi dnevi. Skok je posledica enega mocnega hladnega valov, ki je v gore nad 1.500 m prinesel do 30 cm svežega snega.

p: Pred tednom je samo 90 km² slovenskega visokogorja imelo sneg. Do 16. novembra se je povečalo na 1.130 km². Nato je otoplitev zmanjšala pokrajnost na 260 km² do 18. novembra. Mraz se je vrnil in do 19. novembra je sneg pokrival 760 km² – neto porast 670 km² od začetka tedna.
Takšne nihaje so v zgodnjem novembru normalne: topli valovi stalijo tanek sneg na nižjih pobočjih, hladi valovi ga obnovijo. Pomembno je sedaj, ali se baza obdrži.

Julijci so dobili največ: 55 cm svežega snega v treh dneh. Kamniško-savinjske Alpe so nabrala 46 cm. Pohorje na vzhodu je dobilo samo 3 cm. Približno 400 km² je dobilo najmanj 5 cm, večinoma nad 1.500 m.
Najbolj deževni dan je bil 22. november s količino do 17 cm. To je bil prvi sneg sezone na mnogih krajih.

Višina odloča vse. Pod 1.000 m skoraj nič snega (1 % pokrito, manj kot 1 cm povprečno). Med 1.000 in 1.500 m tanke fleke (13 % pokrito, manj kot 1 cm). Med 1.500 in 2.000 m prava baza: 9 cm povprečno, 96 % pokrito. Nad 2.000 m trdna: 25 cm povprečno, v celoti belo.
Snežna črta se nahaja pri približno 1.400 m. Smučarske proge nad to višino imajo neprekinjeno pokrajnost. Pod njo travišča še vidimo.

sections.h: Globina snega na smučarskih centjih 19. novembra
p: Kranjska Gora drži največ snega med slovenskimi smučarskim centji: 29 cm. To je več od povprečja za konec novembra (običajno 2 cm na ta datum). V zadnjih treh dneh je nabrala 7 cm in do nedelje 22. novembra bi lahko nabrala še 9 cm.

Sella Nevea na višini 2.137 m ima 24 cm – veliko več od običajnih 2 cm za sredo november. V treh dneh je absorbirala 28 cm, nenavadno velik padec za ta majhen center. Do nedelje je napovedanih še do 19 cm.

Ostali: Vogel (12 cm, 8 cm v treh dneh, 17 cm poda), Kope (11 cm, 2 cm v treh dneh, 9 cm poda), Krvavec (8 cm, 17 cm v treh dneh, 22 cm poda). Sneg leži na zgornjih pobočjih 14 od 27 smučarskih centjev na Slovenskem.

Napoved za prihodnji teden: do 35 cm skupaj, 17 cm v naslednjih treh dneh. Po 22. novembru se ritem padavin upočasni. Dnevi 8 do 14 napovedi (konec novembra v zgodnji december) kažejo do 24 cm na najbolj mokrih pobočjih.

Zgodnji sezonski sneg je tanek in leži na golih skalah na mnogih mestih. Pripravljene in uhodane proge so najvarnejše. Sveži sneg na mrazu lahko nestabilen na strmih terenih: pred smučanjem izven prog preberite lokalni plaz bulletin.

sections.h: Kako se to primerja z Avstrijo in Italijo
p: Čez mejo je Avstrija veliko bolj bela: 48 % njenega visokogorja pokrite, Stubaier Gletscher kaže 74 cm. Italija je pri 27 %, vodi La Thuile s 66 cm. Slovenija pri 10 % zaostaja za obema sosedama, toda razlika se bo zaprla, če se napoved izide.

advice: Zaenkrat ostanite na pripravljenih progah: baza pod zgodnjim snegom je tanka in lahko skriva skale.
Če načrtujete smučanje izven prog, preberite lokalni plaz bulletin. Sveži hladni sneg se lahko udre na strmih pobočjih.
Počakajte do 22. novembra, če je le mogoče: sveži sneg se bo usedel in ceste bodo očiščene.
Nad 1.500 m boste našli neprekinjeno pokrajnost; pod 1.000 m pričakujte gole flete.
Vzemite si zemljevid: otoplitev in ponovno zmrzovanje pomenita flekasto snežno pokrajnost na srednji višini (1.000–1.500 m), s samo 13 % belo.

captions.new: Sveži sneg je padel čez Slovenijo v treh dneh do 19. novembra, z vrhom 30 cm v Julijcih in Kamniško-savinjskih Alpah.
captions.map: Snežna pokrajnost 19. novembra: 760 km² slovenskega visokogorja (10 %), koncentrirano nad 1.400 m. Pred sedmimi dnevi je bilo belo samo 90 km².
captions.story: Tednov skok: sneg je pokrival 1.130 km² 16. novembra, padel na 260 km² do 18. novembra s temperaturo, ki je narasla, nato pa se vrnil na 760 km² s povratkom mraza.
